title: 2 Kings Chapter 13 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on 2 Kings chapter 13 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: 2 Kings Chapter 13 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of 2 Kings Chapter 13.

questions.question: In whose reign did Jehoahaz begin to reign over Israel according to 2 Kings 13?
options: Joash, son of Ahaziah king of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: Joash, son of Ahaziah king of Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:1 states that Jehoahaz began to reign in the three and twentieth year of Joash the son of Ahaziah king of Judah.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoahaz did what was right in the sight of the LORD during his reign.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:2 clearly says Jehoahaz did that which was evil in the sight of the LORD and followed the sins of Jeroboam.

questions.question: Who oppressed Israel during the days of Jehoahaz?
options: Hazael king of Syria and his son Benhadad
questions.correctAnswer: Hazael king of Syria and his son Benhadad
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:3 states that the LORD delivered Israel into the hand of Hazael king of Syria and Benhadad his son all their days.

questions.question: What did Jehoahaz do when he saw the oppression of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Besought the LORD
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:4 says Jehoahaz besought the LORD because he saw the oppression of Israel.

questions.question: True or False: The LORD gave Israel a saviour so they went out from under the hand of the Syrians.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:5 confirms that the LORD gave Israel a saviour and they went out from under the hand of the Syrians.

questions.question: Despite being delivered from Syria, what sin did Israel continue to follow?
options: The sins of the house of Jeroboam
questions.correctAnswer: The sins of the house of Jeroboam
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:6 states they departed not from the sins of the house of Jeroboam who made Israel sin.

questions.question: How many horsemen did Jehoahaz have left after the Syrians destroyed much of his people?
questions.correctAnswer: Fifty horsemen
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:7 says Jehoahaz was left with fifty horsemen after the king of Syria destroyed them.

questions.question: Where are the acts and might of Jehoahaz recorded according to the chapter?
options: In the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel
In the book of the prophets
questions.correctAnswer: In the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:8 states that the rest of the acts and might of Jehoahaz are written in the book of the chronicles of the kings of Israel.

questions.question: Who reigned over Israel after Jehoahaz died?
questions.correctAnswer: Joash, his son
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:9 states that Joash his son reigned in his stead after Jehoahaz died.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoash, son of Jehoahaz, began to reign in the thirty and seventh year of Joash king of Judah.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:10 confirms Jehoash began to reign in the thirty and seventh year of Joash king of Judah.

questions.question: What kind of deeds did Jehoash do in the sight of the LORD?
options: Evil deeds, following the sins of Jeroboam
questions.correctAnswer: Evil deeds, following the sins of Jeroboam
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:11 says Jehoash did evil and departed not from the sins of Jeroboam.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 13, whose might did Joash use to fight against Amaziah king of Judah?
questions.correctAnswer: His own might
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:12 states Joash's might wherewith he fought against Amaziah king of Judah is recorded.

questions.question: What did Joash do when Elisha was sick before he died?
options: Came down to him and wept over his face
Sent a messenger with a message
questions.correctAnswer: Came down to him and wept over his face
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:14 says Joash came down unto Elisha and wept over his face.

questions.question: In what order did these events occur in 2 Kings 13: bow and arrows given, Elisha's death, Joash's reign, and Jehoahaz's reign?
options: Jehoahaz's reign, Joash's reign, bow and arrows given, Elisha's death
Joash's reign, Jehoahaz's reign, Elisha's death, bow and arrows given
Elisha's death, bow and arrows given, Jehoahaz's reign, Joash's reign
Bow and arrows given, Jehoahaz's reign, Joash's reign, Elisha's death
questions.correctAnswer: Jehoahaz's reign, Joash's reign, bow and arrows given, Elisha's death
questions.explanation: Jehoahaz reigned first (v1), then Joash reigned (v10), then Joash received bow and arrows from Elisha (v15), and Elisha died thereafter (v20).

questions.question: True or False: Jehoahaz was buried in Jerusalem according to 2 Kings 13.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:9 states Jehoahaz was buried in Samaria, not Jerusalem.

medium.title: 2 Kings Chapter 13 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from 2 Kings Chapter 13 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How long did Jehoash, the son of Jehoahaz, reign over Israel in Samaria?
questions.correctAnswer: 16 years
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:10 states that Jehoash began to reign in the thirty-seventh year of Joash king of Judah and reigned sixteen years.

questions.question: What was Jehoash's spiritual condition during his reign according to 2 Kings 13?
options: He did evil and followed the sins of Jeroboam
He fully obeyed the LORD and reformed Israel
He was neutral in religious matters
He destroyed the groves and served the LORD alone
questions.correctAnswer: He did evil and followed the sins of Jeroboam
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:11 says Jehoash did evil in the sight of the LORD and did not depart from the sins of Jeroboam the son of Nebat.

questions.question: What battle experience of Jehoash is mentioned in 2 Kings 13?
options: He fought against Amaziah king of Judah
He fought against Hazael king of Syria
questions.correctAnswer: He fought against Amaziah king of Judah
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:12 mentions Jehoash's might wherewith he fought against Amaziah king of Judah.

questions.question: Where was Joash buried after his death?
options: In Samaria with the kings of Israel
In Jerusalem with the kings of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: In Samaria with the kings of Israel
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:13 states Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

questions.question: What did King Joash of Israel do when Elisha was sick and near death?
options: He wept over Elisha's face and called him 'O my father'
He sent gifts to Elisha's family
He prayed silently but did not visit
questions.correctAnswer: He wept over Elisha's face and called him 'O my father'
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:14 describes how Joash came down to Elisha, wept over him, and called him 'O my father, my father, the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof.'

questions.question: What did Elisha instruct King Joash to take when he visited him?
questions.correctAnswer: Bow and arrows
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:15 says Elisha told Joash to take bow and arrows, and he took them.

questions.question: What symbolic action did Elisha perform with King Joash's hands on the bow?
options: He put his hands over the king's hands
He handed the bow to a servant
questions.correctAnswer: He put his hands over the king's hands
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:16 states Elisha put his hands upon the king's hands as he put his hand upon the bow.

questions.question: What did Elisha say the arrow shot from the eastward window represented?
options: The arrow of the LORD's deliverance from Syria
A symbol of peace with Syria
questions.correctAnswer: The arrow of the LORD's deliverance from Syria
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:17 explains that Elisha said the arrow was the arrow of the LORD's deliverance from Syria, indicating Israel would smite the Syrians in Aphek until consumed.

questions.question: How many times did King Joash strike the ground with the arrows as instructed by Elisha?
questions.correctAnswer: Three times
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:18 states Joash smote upon the ground thrice and then stayed.

questions.question: What was Elisha's reaction to Joash striking the ground only three times?
options: He was angry and said Joash should have smitten five or six times
He praised Joash for his obedience
He told Joash to stop completely
questions.correctAnswer: He was angry and said Joash should have smitten five or six times
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:19 reveals Elisha was wroth with Joash, saying he should have smitten five or six times to consume Syria fully, but now only thrice.

questions.question: What happened to Elisha after these events?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:20 confirms Elisha died and was buried after these events.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 13, when a man was buried and cast into Elisha's sepulchre, what happened?
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:21 states that when the man was let down and touched the bones of Elisha, he revived and stood on his feet.

questions.question: The passage teaches that incomplete obedience can limit God's blessings, as shown by Joash striking the ground only three times instead of five or six.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:18-19 shows Elisha's rebuke that Joash should have struck five or six times for full victory, illustrating the importance of wholehearted obedience.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 13:19 promise will happen if the king had struck the ground five or six times as Elisha instructed?
options: He would have struck Syria until he had consumed it
He would have lost the battle
He would have angered the LORD
He would have made peace with Syria
questions.correctAnswer: He would have struck Syria until he had consumed it
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:19 says if Joash had smitten five or six times, he would have smitten Syria until it was consumed, connecting the action with complete deliverance.

questions.question: How does the interaction between Elisha and Joash in 2 Kings 13 teach about the virtue of faith and trust in God?
options: It shows that trusting God's instructions fully leads to greater deliverance
It shows faith is unnecessary if one has power
It teaches to rely on weapons rather than God
It suggests partial obedience is enough for blessings
questions.correctAnswer: It shows that trusting God's instructions fully leads to greater deliverance
questions.explanation: The passage (2 Kings 13:14-19) illustrates that full obedience and trust in God's prophetic word bring complete victory, while partial obedience limits blessings.

hard.title: 2 Kings Chapter 13 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from 2 Kings Chapter 13.

questions.question: How many times did Joash strike the ground with arrows as instructed by Elisha?
questions.correctAnswer: Thrice
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:18 states that Joash smote the ground three times, but Elisha was displeased because he should have smitten five or six times for complete victory.

questions.question: What was Elisha's reaction to Joash striking the ground fewer times than instructed?
options: He was pleased with Joash's obedience
He was wroth and rebuked Joash
questions.correctAnswer: He was wroth and rebuked Joash
questions.explanation: According to 2 Kings 13:19, Elisha was angry because Joash struck only thrice instead of five or six times, which limited the defeat of Syria.

questions.question: What happened to a man who touched the bones of Elisha during burial rites?
options: He revived and stood on his feet
questions.correctAnswer: He revived and stood on his feet
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:21 describes that when a dead man was thrown into Elisha’s sepulchre and touched his bones, the man came back to life and stood up.

questions.question: Who succeeded Hazael as king of Syria?
questions.correctAnswer: Benhadad, his son
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:24 records that after Hazael died, his son Benhadad reigned in his stead over Syria.

questions.question: How many times did Joash defeat Benhadad and recover cities of Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Thrice
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:25 says Joash beat Benhadad three times, recovering the cities taken from his father’s reign.

questions.question: What does the phrase 'the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof' refer to in Elisha's lament?
options: Divine protection and strength of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Divine protection and strength of Israel
questions.explanation: In 2 Kings 13:14, Joash calls Elisha 'the chariot of Israel, and the horsemen thereof,' a metaphor for God's power and protection through Elisha’s prophetic ministry.

questions.question: Which covenant is cited as the reason God showed compassion to Israel despite their sins?
options: The covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
questions.correctAnswer: The covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:23 states that God's compassion came because of His covenant with the patriarchs Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

questions.question: What literary device is illustrated by Elisha’s rebuke of Joash striking the ground three times instead of five or six?
questions.correctAnswer: Foreshadowing
questions.explanation: Elisha's rebuke (2 Kings 13:19) foreshadows an incomplete military victory due to Joash's partial obedience, illustrating the broader theme of Israel's limited success caused by incomplete faithfulness.

questions.question: How does the revival of the dead man touching Elisha’s bones relate to New Testament themes?
options: It is unrelated to New Testament themes
questions.correctAnswer: It prefigures resurrection through Jesus
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:21’s miracle prefigures resurrection, a central New Testament theme fulfilled in Christ’s resurrection (cf. John 11:25).

questions.question: What is the meaning of the Hebrew word translated as 'smite' in the context of striking the ground with arrows?
questions.correctAnswer: To strike or hit
questions.explanation: The Hebrew verb 'nakah' translated as 'smite' generally means to strike or hit, emphasizing the physical act Joash was to perform on the ground (2 Kings 13:18).

questions.question: Which king oppressed Israel during the days of Jehoahaz according to this chapter?
questions.correctAnswer: Hazael
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:22 states that Hazael king of Syria oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz.

questions.question: What historical context helps explain the oppression of Israel by Syria during Jehoahaz’s reign?
questions.correctAnswer: Syrian military expansion under Hazael
questions.explanation: The chapter (2 Kings 13:3) mentions Hazael king of Syria delivering Israel into his hand, reflecting the period of Syrian military aggression and expansion in the 9th century BCE.

questions.question: True or False: Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:13 explicitly states Joash was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel.

questions.question: True or False: Jehoahaz fully obeyed Elisha’s instructions and struck the ground five or six times.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: 2 Kings 13:18–19 records that Jehoahaz struck the ground only three times, and Elisha was displeased, saying he should have struck five or six times.

questions.question: Which other Old Testament passage echoes the theme of God's covenant compassion despite Israel's sin as seen in 2 Kings 13:23?
questions.correctAnswer: Deuteronomy 7:7-9
questions.explanation: Deuteronomy 7:7-9 speaks of God's covenant love and faithfulness to Israel despite their unworthiness, echoing 2 Kings 13:23's theme of covenant compassion.

theological.title: 2 Kings Chapter 13 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from 2 Kings Chapter 13 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine is exemplified by the LORD's repeated deliverance of Israel despite their ongoing sin in 2 Kings 13:4-5 and 23?
options: The doctrine of divine grace and covenant faithfulness
The doctrine of human free will
questions.correctAnswer: The doctrine of divine grace and covenant faithfulness
questions.explanation: Verses 4-5 show God responding to Israel's pleas by delivering them from Syrian oppression, and verse 23 highlights God's compassion and covenant faithfulness despite Israel's sin. This teaches that God's grace and His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob sustain Israel.

questions.question: Which attribute of God is most clearly demonstrated in 2 Kings 13:23 where He continues to have compassion on Israel despite their sins?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s mercy
questions.explanation: Verse 23 explicitly states that the LORD was gracious and had compassion on Israel, showing His merciful nature even when His people persist in sin.

questions.question: According to 2 Kings 13:2 and 11, what persistent sin did the kings Jehoahaz and Joash commit that led Israel into repeated judgment?
options: Following the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat
questions.correctAnswer: Following the sins of Jeroboam son of Nebat
questions.explanation: Both verses 2 and 11 highlight that Jehoahaz and Jehoash continued the sins of Jeroboam, which were the cause of Israel's spiritual downfall.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 13:14-17 present Elisha's role in relation to Israel’s kings, and what does this reveal about prophetic mediation in the Old Testament?
options: Elisha acts as a military commander directing battles
Elisha functions as a mediator conveying God’s promises of deliverance
Elisha judges the kings for their sins
Elisha performs miracles to punish Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Elisha functions as a mediator conveying God’s promises of deliverance
questions.explanation: In these verses, Elisha instructs King Joash to shoot arrows symbolizing the LORD’s deliverance from Syria, revealing the prophet’s role as God’s mediator to the king.

questions.question: What theological lesson can be drawn from the incident in 2 Kings 13:21 where a dead man revived upon touching Elisha’s bones?
options: The power of relics in Old Testament worship
The holiness and continuing power of God’s prophet even after death
That resurrection was common in Israel’s history
questions.correctAnswer: The holiness and continuing power of God’s prophet even after death
questions.explanation: Verse 21 shows that the power of God worked through Elisha’s bones to bring a man back to life, signifying the enduring holiness and divine power associated with God’s prophets.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 13:7 reveal about the consequences of Israel’s sin for its military strength?
options: Israel’s army was greatly diminished by the king of Syria
Israel expanded its military might despite sin
Israel’s military was unaffected by spiritual failures
Israel formed alliances to strengthen its army
questions.correctAnswer: Israel’s army was greatly diminished by the king of Syria
questions.explanation: Verse 7 states that only fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand footmen remained because the king of Syria had destroyed much of Israel’s forces, showing the temporal consequences of sin on national security.

questions.question: How does 2 Kings 13:25 demonstrate God’s sovereignty over nations even through human conflict?
options: Israel’s success came from their own strength only
Joash’s repeated victories over Benhadad show God’s control over geopolitical events
questions.correctAnswer: Joash’s repeated victories over Benhadad show God’s control over geopolitical events
questions.explanation: Verse 25 describes Joash defeating Benhadad three times and recovering cities, illustrating that God ordains the rise and fall of nations as part of His providential plan.

questions.question: What combined theological insight about sin and deliverance is taught by 2 Kings 13:6 and 11 regarding Israel’s spiritual condition?
options: Israel’s complete repentance led to lasting peace
Persistent sin leads to persistent judgment despite temporary deliverance
The sins of Jeroboam were forgiven
questions.correctAnswer: Persistent sin leads to persistent judgment despite temporary deliverance
questions.explanation: Verse 6 shows Israel did not depart from Jeroboam’s sins despite being delivered, and verse 11 states Jehoash continued those sins, teaching that ongoing disobedience results in ongoing divine discipline.

questions.question: What does 2 Kings 13:18-19 teach about human obedience in relation to divine promises through Elisha's rebuke of King Joash?
options: Partial obedience limits the fullness of God’s blessing
God accepts any level of obedience
Obedience is irrelevant to God’s plans
The king’s actions had no consequences
questions.correctAnswer: Partial obedience limits the fullness of God’s blessing
questions.explanation: In verses 18-19, Elisha rebukes Joash for striking the ground only three times instead of five or six, indicating that incomplete obedience results in limited victory over Syria.

questions.question: How does the account of Jehoahaz’s reign in 2 Kings 13:1-3 and 22 reveal the interplay between divine judgment and human agency?
options: Divine judgment happens regardless of human action
Human kings control their own fate fully
God allows foreign oppression as judgment for Israel’s sin, yet human kings also enact decisions within that framework
The king of Syria acted independently of God
questions.correctAnswer: God allows foreign oppression as judgment for Israel’s sin, yet human kings also enact decisions within that framework
questions.explanation: Verses 1-3 and 22 show that because of Israel’s sin, God delivered them into the hand of Syrian kings, demonstrating that divine judgment operates through human agents.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that Old Testament narratives portray God as arbitrary in His punishment. What does 2 Kings 13:2-5 and 23 actually teach about God's justice and mercy?
options: God’s punishment is a measured response to persistent sin, coupled with mercy upon repentance
questions.correctAnswer: God’s punishment is a measured response to persistent sin, coupled with mercy upon repentance
questions.explanation: Verses 2-5 and 23 show that God’s anger is kindled because of Israel’s sin, leading to judgment through Syrian oppression, but He also hears their pleas and shows compassion, demonstrating both justice and mercy.

questions.question: What narrative role does the death of Elisha in 2 Kings 13:20-21 play in the broader redemptive storyline of Scripture?
options: It marks the end of all prophetic activity
It foreshadows resurrection power through God’s prophet, prefiguring Christ’s resurrection
It indicates the failure of prophecy
It signifies the end of Israel’s monarchy
questions.correctAnswer: It foreshadows resurrection power through God’s prophet, prefiguring Christ’s resurrection
questions.explanation: Elisha’s death in verse 20 followed by the revival of a dead man upon touching his bones in verse 21 symbolically anticipates resurrection power, a theme fulfilled in Christ’s resurrection.

questions.question: What synthesis of doctrine emerges from 2 Kings 13:14-17 and 18-19 about God’s deliverance and human responsibility?
options: God acts independently of human effort
Human obedience is irrelevant to divine promises
God’s deliverance is assured but requires human cooperation and obedience
questions.correctAnswer: God’s deliverance is assured but requires human cooperation and obedience
questions.explanation: Verses 14-17 show God’s promise of deliverance through Elisha’s symbolic arrow, while verses 18-19 emphasize the king’s failure to fully obey limiting victory, teaching that divine promise requires human response.

questions.question: How do the reigns of Jehoahaz and Jehoash in 2 Kings 13:1-11 and 24-25 contribute to the biblical narrative of covenant unfaithfulness and partial restoration?
options: They represent total obedience to God
Their reigns highlight ongoing covenant unfaithfulness but also God’s provision of military restoration
questions.correctAnswer: Their reigns highlight ongoing covenant unfaithfulness but also God’s provision of military restoration
questions.explanation: These verses show both kings persisting in Jeroboam’s sins (unfaithfulness) but also experiencing military successes granted by God (partial restoration), fitting the pattern of covenant judgment and mercy.

questions.question: What attribute of God is revealed in 2 Kings 13:23 when He chooses not to destroy Israel despite their sins, citing His covenant with the patriarchs?
questions.correctAnswer: God’s faithfulness
questions.explanation: Verse 23 shows that God’s actions are governed by His covenant promises to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, revealing His unchanging faithfulness.
